newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan amends bank law to allow Islamic banking.
newsitem.headline: Jordan amends bank law to allow Islamic banking.

text.p: Jordan's parliament has passed an amendment to the existing banking law to allow the Central Bank to license Islamic banks in addition to other commercial banks, bankers said on Thursday.

They said the amendment should help break a monopoly held by the Jordan Islamic Bank which is the country's only Islamic Bank. It is governed by a special law in 1978 under which it specifies that it operates under Islamic non-interest bearing rules.
But because of Islamist lobbying the new amendment does not allow the Central Bank to license Islamic offshoots of existing commercial banks.

Jordan has 21 licensed banks including six investment banks and five subsidiaries of foreign banks with total deposits -- both local and foreign currency -- of around 5.973 billion dinars ($8.45 billion).
